shots.caption: An animation introduces the title question 'How does an mRNA vaccine work?' as coronavirus particles float into view across the screen.
on_screen_text: HOW DOES AN mRNA VACCINE WORK?
shots.action: Displaying the title text as coronavirus illustrations enter and multiply across the background.

shots.caption: An animation illustrates how a coronavirus attaches to a cell, followed by a syringe introducing an mRNA molecule into a cell.
shots.action: Demonstrating viral attachment to a cell and subsequent delivery of mRNA into a cell using an animated syringe.

shots.caption: The animation shows the cell producing harmless COVID spikes, which trigger an immune cell to generate specific antibodies.
shots.action: Depicting spike protein production and immune cell activation leading to antibody generation.

shots.caption: Antibodies cluster around and neutralize the coronavirus, concluding with credits and institutional attribution.
on_screen_text: Research provided by Barry Bloom Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
entities: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
shots.action: Illustrating antibody neutralization of the virus followed by closing credit title cards.
